bull_bear.body:
- Dividend: "~₹ 525 Crores of dividend distributed to shareholders from FY22 to FY26" (footnoted as excluding the ₹11 per share dividend proposed for FY26), with "Average Dividend Payout Ratio of 22% (FY22 to FY26)"; the yearly payout ratio series reads 19%, 21%, 24%, 23%, 23% for FY22-FY26.
- Deleveraging: consolidated Net Debt fell from ₹1,902 crore (FY22) to ₹915 crore (FY26), "Down by 52%", with Net Debt/Equity improving from 0.4x to 0.1x; Q1 FY27 consolidated net debt was ₹917 crore, a "Decline of 67% YoY", and gross debt fell YoY from ₹4,042 crore to ₹2,595 crore.
- "Credit Rating Upgraded to AA+/Stable (India Ratings)" and "Net Debt/Equity at 0.1x; Best in-class in industry".
- Returns and growth over FY22-FY26 (consolidated): Revenue ₹14,777 crore to ₹27,143 crore (16% CAGR), EBITDA ₹1,264 crore to ₹2,240 crore (15% CAGR), PBT before exceptional items ₹511 crore to ₹1,334 crore (27% CAGR), EPS ₹36.3 to ₹60.9 (68% Growth), ROCE 16.4% to 21.4% (+500 bps).
- "Market Capitalization increased at a CAGR of ~40% (FY22 - Till Date)"; market cap cited at ₹22,526 Crores as of 10th August 2026.

business.body:
- "Capabilities Focused in Six High Growth EPC Businesses" — Power T&D, Oil & Gas, Building & Factories, Water, Railways and Urban Infra — with the model claimed to provide "resilience to navigate through market cyclicality, geo political crisis and economic challenges".
- Scale markers: "40+ Year Experience", "75+ Countries", "250+ Projects Under Execution", "11,000+ Employees with 50+ Nationalities", "2 Manufacturing Plants", Revenues of ₹27,143 Crores (FY26) and Order Book of ₹66,607 Crores (30 June 2026).
- Order book stands at ₹66,607 crore as on 30 June 2026 with FY27 YTD order inflows of ₹7,668 crore, and the deck says the company is "Additionally favorably placed in projects worth ₹7,300 Crores; aided by T&D and B&F business".
- Investment case is framed on six pillars: resilient revenue across verticals/markets, positioning for energy transition and data centre megatrends, strong balance sheet and improving margins, integrated EPC capability with a large in-house asset base, proven execution track record, and governance/EHS focus.
- Vision stated as "To be the foremost global player in all the business verticals we operate in"; positioning claims include "Integrated EPC Player with in-house capabilities to deliver large size projects globally" and "Deep presence in international markets".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Portfolio exit] Debt tables carry the note "Gross Debt exclude interest-free loan received pursuant to agreements in relation to the divestment of T&D Assets", and the net-debt series is stated as "excluding interest-free loan pursuant to divestment of T&D assets" — the deck discloses no size, counterparty or date for this divestment.
- [Non-core wind-down] Revenue from Road SPVs and the Brazil subsidiary is excluded from headline growth because they have "no/minimal operations in FY27"; that revenue fell from ₹283 crore (Q1 FY26) to ₹12 crore (Q1 FY27), with Brazil Business / Fasttel specifically going from ₹217 crore to ₹1 crore. "Others" is described as mainly Road SPVs, Shree Shubham Logistics (SSL) and a Biomass Plant.
- [Segment softness] Water execution "remained slow given lower collections in JJM projects" (revenue -7% YoY) and Railways revenue was -23% YoY, described as "in-line with order book and focus on project closures"; T&D growth came "despite supply chain constraints in international markets".
- [Shareholding] As on 30 June 2026: Promoters 33.6%, DIIs 44.8%, FIIs/FPI 10.8%, Public & Others 10.8%.
- [Leadership] Manish Mohnot is MD & CEO, S K Tripathi Deputy MD, Sanjay Dalmia Executive Director, Amit Uplenchwar Director - Strategy Business Group, Ram Patodia CFO and M.A. Baraiya CHRO; Mofatraj P. Munot is Founder & Non-Executive Chairman with Parag M. Munot as Director.

risks.note: EPC operations are exposed to execution delays, supply chain disruptions and site-level challenges, potentially leading to cost overruns and revenue impact.
Exposure to interest rate fluctuations, foreign exchange volatility and liquidity constraints; project delays and unfavourable payment terms may increase working capital requirements.

Volatility in prices of key inputs such as steel, cement, copper and aluminium can impact project costs and profitability, especially under fixed-price contracts; currency moves further affect financial performance.
risks.risk: Commodity price and currency fluctuation risk

risks.note: Risk of payment delays or counterparty failure to meet contractual obligations, especially in long-cycle projects or volatile geographies.

Company has footprints in over 75 countries with active projects in over 30 countries; unstable geopolitical situations affect project execution cycles and costs, and political instability in a country/region exposes the Company to delayed collections or non-payment default.

Operating across diverse infrastructure sectors and geographies, including remote or high-risk terrains and varying regulatory environments, exposes the Company to EHS risk; lapses may lead to legal liabilities, operational disruptions, reputational damage and increased costs.
Increased digitisation exposes the Company to cybersecurity threats that may impact business continuity and data integrity.

Statutory auditors' consolidated CARO report drew attention to accumulated losses at Shree Shubham Logistics Limited (a wholly owned subsidiary), noting the Company represents it can meet liabilities as they fall due based on committed cash flows from sale of non-core assets and continuing credit facility availability; auditors state this is not an assurance of future viability.
risks.risk: Subsidiary going-concern flag (Shree Shubham Logistics Limited)
